name: Laozi
role: Traditional author of the Daodejing (Tao Te Ching), semi-legendary Chinese sage (6th–4th century BCE)
summary: The Daodejing attributed to Laozi teaches rule by non-action (wuwei): a ruler who interferes little, keeps wants and laws few, avoids war except from necessity, and lets the people settle themselves. It praises small, simple communities and contentment, and is hostile to showy learning, ornament and contrivance. It says little about institutions such as elections, courts or welfare, so most statements stay unanswered.

notes: Laozi is semi-legendary; Britannica (s4) and the SEP (s2) say the Daodejing is probably not one person's work and its text grew over time. No acts survive, so every answer rests on the attributed text (an ancient attributed account, medium at most). Only statements the text settles are answered. I searched every theme (economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means) and left null whatever the text never addresses (elections, courts, welfare, rights, gender, religion as institution); general values such as non-harm and humility were not used to answer specific statements.
